adds.title: Inmate at women's prison files suit over housing of transgender prisoner (Sun Journal, Maine)
adds.summary: Sun Journal (3 Apr 2026, Mark LaFlamme) documents that Maine Corrections housed Andrea Balcer, a 27-year-old transgender woman and convicted double murderer, in the women's facility (Maine Correctional Center, Windham) for at least a year as of April 2026 - i.e. placement by current gender identity rather than birth sex. Inmate Katie Mountain (41) filed a 30-page complaint on 3 Apr 2026 against MDOC Commissioner Randall Liberty, Warden Ben Beal and Balcer, alleging chronic harassment and assault by the trans prisoner; attorney Cynthia Dill filed it. Outcome pending (complaint filed, no ruling reported in the article); the harassment/assault claims are allegations, while the placement fact - a trans woman held in the women's prison - is documented.

records.note: 1 verified add (thin but placement-documented): Maine DOC has been housing a transgender woman in the women's facility at Maine Correctional Center (Windham) for at least a year as of April 2026, per the Sun Journal's report of the lawsuit filed 3 Apr 2026 (Katie Mountain v. Commissioner Liberty, Warden Beal, Balcer; attorney Cynthia Dill). No trans special units, no solitary/segregation practice for trans prisoners, and no contrary (birth-sex) placement rule were found in the fetched sources within budget.
